title: Meridian handoff: friction notes and quick triage
content:
Quick context
- I'm logging this mid-meridian shift because a few recurring friction points surfaced and I want them captured before the late shift. Mostly small operational gotchas that compound when combined (KV cache invalidation + routing fallback + private region cold instances).

Summary of issues observed today
1) KV prefix invalidation delay (~45s)
   - Symptom: old completions returned for rare user prefix during heavy load. Not full regression but noticeable (~0.8% of requests in a 10m window).
   - First-line check: logs for cache-miss vs cache-hit on serving node (grep for prefix_hash in /var/log/runtime/access.log).
   - Workaround used: forced local cache flush (systemctl restart redwood-cache on affected pod) which reduced recurrence.
   - Root-cause hypothesis: eviction race under async background compaction + heavy batching. File a followup (JIRA-8243).

2) Model fallback hitting older quantized variant unexpectedly
   - Symptom: requests routed to model-x-v1-qat instead of v2-quant when dedicated cluster transiently full. v1 emits hallucinated special tokens (known behavioral regression).
   - Quick mitigation: pin route to v2-quant by setting route_override header in the API gateway for traffic from the affected customer (see curl snippet below).
   - Longer term: ensure canary tags and compatibility matrix in routing-service are considered during fallback. Follow-up PR pending (runtime PR #1887).

3) Private deployment flaky DNS on warmup
   - Symptom: after autoscale event, some instances fail healthchecks due to dns lookup timeouts for internal-kms (customer-managed).
   - Immediate step: run dig + retry with host entries temporarily in /etc/hosts for critical endpoints while we wait for upstream DNS caches to populate. Documented in Confluence link above.

Quick triage checklist (what I actually ran during shift)
- Confirm alert: check PagerDuty alert payload + top-level error group id.
- Check global routing SLOs: https://console.redwood.com/ops/slo (look for region spikes).
- Identify affected customers (tenant_id in logs).
- Tail logs on serving nodes: kubectl -n inference logs -l app=runtime -f --tail=200 | grep <error_group>
- Check KV cache metrics: prometheus query = rate(redwood_kv_gets_total[5m]) vs redwood_kv_evictions_total
- If cache inconsistency suspected: restart redwood-cache on the smallest superset of pods that reproduce; avoid cluster-wide restarts.

Useful commands (copy paste)
- Pin route for a single key temporarily:
  curl -X POST 
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN' 
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' 
    https://gateway.redwood.internal/v1/routes/override 
    -d '{"tenant":"my-tenant","route":"/generate","model":"model-x-v2-quant","duration_secs":300}'

- Tail logs for prefix hash (replace PHASH):
  kubectl -n inference exec -it $(kubectl -n inference get pod -l app=router -o jsonpath='{.items[0].metadata.name}') -- sh -c "tail -n 500 /var/log/runtime/access.log | grep PHASH"

- Force local cache restart (avoid blanket restarts)
  kubectl -n inference rollout restart deployment/redwood-cache --selector=region=us-west-2 - but prefer single-pod restart via kubectl exec systemctl restart redwood-cache

Escalation notes (if the above doesn't help)
- Page eng-oncall (PD urgent) if >5% error rate sustained for 5m or customer-impacting requests fail end-to-end.
- When paging, include: recent routing decisions (snapshot of routing-service state), affected cluster ids, and recent cache metrics.
- If private deployment involved, page the oncall for infra-private (Aisha) and include contact for customer infra team. There's an established DM channel: slack://user/Aisha (linked above).

Observations & friction (things to consider at handoff)
- The routing fallback logic is very sensitive to instantaneous cluster free slots. During spikes, it will pick the first compatible variant even if that variant has known regressions. We should add a weight penalty for historically regressed variants.
- Cache compaction is scheduled aggressively at night; but under continuous batchy workloads it triggers mid-day and contends with request path. Consider moving compaction to lower priority threads or coordinating with autoscaler to reduce churn.
- Private KMS timeouts are a recurring friction point — every private customer with self-managed KMS needs a prewarm plan. Might be a sales/ops checklist item.

Handoff checklist for the next person
- Check PagerDuty for any ongoing alerts. If none, glance at two dashboards: "KV cache health (last 30m)" and "Routing fallback rates (last 15m)". Links in linked_artifacts.
- If you restart any cache pod, leave a note in the incident thread with pod name + reason. Don't do blanket restarts.
- Keep the route override window minimal (5-10m) and revert after stabilizing. PMs hate long pins.
- If the issue looks like repeated fallback to v1 variants, do not re-enable canary traffic to v1 until PR #1887 lands; it's tracked in runtime repo.

Open questions / TODOs
- Can we expose per-tenant fallback-weight metrics? would make noisy tenants visible. (Follow up with routing-service team).
- Add an automated small-sample A/B check that runs after fallback to verify output quality quickly (sanity prompts).
- Investigate moving compaction to a lower CPU share class and test under synthetic batcher load.

Notes to the next shift (free-form)
- If you see a small uptick in latency but no errors, check for recent config changes (rollout notes). Last rollout was 2025-02-10 for batcher v3.
- If a customer complains about hallucinations, ask whether they saw the old special tokens ("<UNK-SYM>") — that's a quick signal it came from v1 variant.
- Coffee recommendation: the 3rd floor breakroom machine is fixed, bring exact change. :)

---
If you pick this up and want me to run a deeper dive, ping me @pri.varma on Slack. Leaving this as a scratch-first draft — will formalize into a Confluence post if patterns repeat.
